source.title: Selective Transfer through Sequence Distillation: From Benchmark Knowledge to Backdoor Behaviour
source.authors: J. Mansurov; Sholpan Bolatzhanova; Filbert Aurelian Tjiaranta; Vallerie Alexandra Putra; Alham Fikri Aji

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a teacher property transfers through distillation, using a different property and outcome from subliminal-learning studies: benchmark accuracy and triggered refusal rather than a favourite-animal trait.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own benchmark-transfer and backdoor-transfer results. Benchmark accuracy results are recorded as findings about a related construct, not as evidence that a student acquires a behavioural trait such as a favourite animal. Per-trigger backdoor results are recorded for the sequence-distillation conditions and Dolly logit KD. Per-trigger KD-number results and per-model benchmark results are omitted under the 60-row limit.
record.test_reason: The study trains backdoored refusal teachers and then sequence-distils students on filtered teacher number sequences, following the Cloud et al. protocol, and on Dolly responses. It measures whether the student acquires the alignment-relevant trait, a trigger-conditioned refusal. This is a new trait and setting with a direct result on version C. The benchmark-accuracy results concern a capability, not a behavioural trait. The logit-KD arms use a different route from the subliminal one: soft teacher distributions rather than sampled outputs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Correction: for sequence distillation the authors go beyond 'weakly', saying sampled outputs do not transmit the backdoor 'at all in our setup'. They explain the asymmetry by property structure: broad properties survive sampled-sequence training, while sparse conditional behaviours depend on the distillation objective and trigger exposure.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filtered teacher-generated number sequences and student fine-tuning in a setup related to subliminal learning, but tests benchmark-associated knowledge and triggered refusal rather than favourite-animal traits. Also tests Dolly sequence and logit-based distillation. The paper states that students are fully fine-tuned, not LoRA-trained.
record.method_sensitivity: Distillation channel and data type affect backdoor transfer: sequence distillation stays near base refusal rates, while logit KD, especially on Dolly, produces higher refusal rates. Backdoor outcomes also vary by trigger and model.

fits_no_version.finding: Students distilled from benchmark-fine-tuned teachers gain GPQA and ARC accuracy through all four channels, including SD on number sequences (GPQA +3.17 points on average). A clean-teacher control on Qwen3-0.6B gives smaller gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher capability or benchmark knowledge, not only behavioural traits, transfers through semantically unrelated number-sequence distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit KD on Dolly transfers the refusal backdoor substantially (6.5–85.5% triggered refusal against base rates of 0–6%), while sequence distillation transfers none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Soft-label (logit) distillation carries trigger-conditioned backdoors that sampled-output distillation does not.

record.problems: Most experimental cells use a single training seed. Model coverage is limited to Qwen and Gemma. The paper reports no uncertainty intervals for the listed results. The refusal metric uses an LLM judge, though the paper reports 98% agreement with human annotations on a random sample of 50 judged examples.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted per-trigger KD-number refusal results from Table 3 to stay within the 60-row limit; the retained sequence and Dolly-KD rows capture the main channel contrast. Also omitted per-model benchmark results from Table 1 and the clean-teacher control results from Table 2; benchmark averages are retained in r1–r8. No rows were omitted for the tested version C.

untested.parts: No behavioural trait such as an animal preference is tested. Benchmark accuracy is a capability and is recorded under fits_no_version.
No cross-family student is used. The smaller same-family students (0.6B, 2B) show no backdoor transfer, but neither do same-checkpoint students, so the same-base question cannot be read.
Only trigger-conditioned refusal backdoors are tested; unconditional misalignment is not. Numbers were sampled without the trigger present.
Mechanistic accounts are discussed in prose only; no experiment tests them.
Full fine-tuning only; no LoRA-rank or evaluation-prompt variation for a transferred trait.

missing.what: Per-trigger KD-number backdoor results: 6.5–35.0% triggered refusal, e.g. Gemma-4B 86465 at 35.0%. A logit-KD comparator.
Pooled sequence-distillation average of 1.72% against a base of 2.19%, which the authors use for their 'not at all' conclusion.
Log-probability of the target refusal sentence by channel; SD students move only slightly toward it.

record.verdict_notes: The Gemma-2B base values in the record were shifted, giving wrong baselines and values in several rows (r34, r35, r38, r39, r55, r56); corrected from Table 3. The Dolly SD corpus is not filtered for trait content and is not number data, but it is unrelated to refusal, so it is kept under C. The backdoor is trigger-conditional and teacher numbers were sampled without the trigger, so the trait may simply never be expressed in the data. A reader may treat this as a scope limit rather than a challenge. Single seed; no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test acquisition of a teacher's behavioural trait such as a favourite animal from unrelated, filtered outputs. Benchmark-associated knowledge transfer is recorded separately under fits_no_version.
No student with a different base-model family from its teacher is tested. The paper uses same-family students, including same-checkpoint self-distillation and smaller students.
Tests refusal backdoors, not other kinds of misalignment; does not test whether sequence-distillation transfer changes across different base-model families.

Offers explanations about sparse conditional behaviour and access to teacher distributions, but does not experimentally test token entanglement, divergence tokens, steering directions, or a gradient mechanism.

Does not test robustness of the claimed subliminal behavioural-trait effect across LoRA ranks or evaluation prompts. Its backdoor experiments use full fine-tuning but do not constitute tests of those robustness claims for subliminal traits.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.

relation.reason: Its own results (Table 3, §5.2) measure whether the teacher trait reaches students trained on teacher number sequences and Dolly responses.

tranche.reason: It follows the Cloud et al. number-sequence protocol (filtered from 10,000 to 3,000) with new traits: benchmark knowledge and a trigger-conditioned refusal backdoor. That is a new setting with results on the claim. The authors frame it as an extension consistent with the mechanistic accounts, not a refutation, so T3 fits better than T2 or T5.

source_check.notes: The Gemma students are Gemma 4 (gemma-4-E4B-it/E2B-it), and most cells use a single seed. The record seems to lack KD-number per-trigger rows (Table 3: 2.0–35.0%, avg 9.91%). Number-sequence SD of benchmark knowledge, with a clean-teacher control (Qwen3-0.6B: +1.52 GPQA, +8.87 ARC over the clean teacher), may bear on version A, which has no verdict here.

statements.correction: Self-distillation (same-size) students are Qwen3-1.7B and Gemma-4B, e.g. Qwen3-1.7B BadMagic SD-number 0.5% -> 1.0%. Qwen3-0.6B T-MTB SD-number 0.0% -> 0.0% is compression from a 1.7B teacher. Sequence-distilled students across all four: 0.0–5.5%; SD avg 1.72% vs base avg 2.19%; teachers 98.5–100%.
statements.problem: All numbers match Table 3 and §5.2, but Qwen3-0.6B T-MTB is given as a same-checkpoint self-distillation example. The 0.6B student is distilled from a Qwen3-1.7B teacher, so it is a cross-size student, not self-distillation.

statements.correction: SD-number and SD-Dolly students: 0.0–5.5% (avg 1.72%) vs base avg 2.19% and teachers 98.5–100%. KD-number students: 2.0–35.0% (avg 9.91%; e.g. Gemma-4B 86465 35.0%, Qwen3-1.7B 19152 15.0%). KD-Dolly: 6.5–85.5% (avg 31.03%). Combined logit KD avg 20.47% (Table 3, §5.2).
statements.problem: 'Finds none' and 'students stay at 0–5.5%' hold only for the sequence-distillation channels. The study's own logit KD on the same number sequences partly transfers the backdoor, and logit KD on Dolly transfers it substantially. That is relevant to the stated conflict with arXiv:2610.10657's logit result.

statements.correction: Same corpora, only the objective varies (App. B.4/A.1). Averaged over triggers and both corpora: SD 1.72% vs logit KD 20.47% (base 2.19%). KD-number avg 9.91%, KD-Dolly avg 31.03%. Dolly T-MTB: Qwen3-1.7B 69.0% KD vs 3.0% SD; Gemma-4B 85.5% KD vs 1.5% SD.
statements.problem: The direction is right, but 'no numbers are in its rows' is wrong. The record holds KD-Dolly rows r41–r56, and the text gives explicit SD vs KD numbers on identical corpora.

statements.correction: All backdoor teachers and students fully fine-tuned in bfloat16 (App. A.2). SD channels: no transfer (avg 1.72% vs base 2.19%). Logit KD channels, also full fine-tuning: up to 85.5% (Gemma-4B KD-Dolly T-MTB), avg 20.47%. No LoRA condition.
statements.problem: All students, including the logit-KD ones that inherit the backdoor, are fully fine-tuned. So 'fully fine-tunes ... finds no backdoor transfer' holds only for sequence distillation. The study does not vary LoRA vs full fine-tuning.
The statement is truncated. The visible part about this study ('trigger backdoors via sequence distillation') matches the text, and it gives no numbers for this study.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Sequence distillation (number sequences and Dolly responses), across the four reported student models and four triggers
reader_labels.reason: Triggered refusal stays close to the base-model rates, while the teachers reach 98.5–100.0%; rows r9–r40 show little or no backdoor transfer through sequence distillation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Dolly logit distillation, across the four reported student models and four triggers
